title: Lesson 1 · What Claude actually is
musicPrompt: Warm, curious workshop bed for a 64-second lesson, about 95 BPM, soft marimba and pizzicato plucks, light woodblock ticks, a gentle bass, a small lift at the rabbit rhyme around 31 seconds and a quiet resolve into the end card, instrumental, no vocals.

scenes.text: Claude isn't a search engine. It's guessing the next word, over and over.
Welcome to Claude Lab, by Curiously.
Claude is built on a large language model, made by Anthropic.
Like your phone's keyboard guessing your next word, but trained on a mountain of text.
You ask. It reads everything so far, picks a likely next word, adds it, and goes again.
It doesn't read out a stored answer. Even with web search, it writes the reply itself.
And it plans. In 2025, Anthropic looked inside a Claude model writing a rhyme. It picked the ending, rabbit, before starting the line.
When researchers switched off rabbit, it wrote habit instead.
So every answer is written fresh, one guess at a time.
But Claude doesn't even read words.
In the next episode, we'll talk about tokens.
